question_record.context: A security incident involving the execution of a known credential theft tool was detected on host `vnevado-win10v`. A file named `mimikatz.exe` was executed with the intention to dump users' credentials, keys, and plain-text passwords. The process ID for this execution was 5196, and it was initiated by an account with the name `tgs2z`.
question_record.question: During further investigation, a SID history injection was detected. Can you determine the AadUserId of the account involved in this malicious activity?
solution: A credential theft tool execution was detected, targeting the account with AadUserId `1d94aaf6-efe6-4e76-ad56-ffd7d1257bc1`.
Activity indicative of the use of the Rubeus kerberoasting tool was identified, involving the process `powershell.exe`.
A Security IDentifcation (SID) history injection was detected, involving the account with AadUserId `7fcf9695-68fc-4258-864d-e1e5b166c66f`.

89.name: Malicious credential theft tool execution detected
89.description:
A known credential theft tool execution command line was detected.
Either the process itself or its command line indicated an intent to dump users' credentials, keys, plain-text passwords and more.

107.name: Possible use of the Rubeus kerberoasting tool
107.description:
Activity indicating the use of the Rubeus tool was observed on this endpoint. This tool can perform kerberoasting, pass-the-ticket, and other attack techniques that take advantage of Kerberos authentication.

During these attacks, attackers often request Kerberos tickets for an account's service principal name (SPN). They then decrypt the tickets to get plaintext credentials associated with the account. Alternatively, they can perform the pass-the-ticket technique to authenticate directly without having to decrypt the obtained tickets.

93.name: SID history injection
93.description: A Security IDentifcation (SID) history injection was detected on this device. SID history is an attribute that supports migration scenarios. Attackers typically use attack tools to change the SID history of an existing domain user to an SID with elevated privileges. With elevated privileges, the affected process might be able to access sensitive files, ensure persistence, and modify system settings.

interpretation.scope: official graph witness, not a proof of causality, actor identity or autonomous planning

steps.sql:
SELECT DISTINCT o.AlertId, o.AlertTitle, o.ObservedAt, o.EntityIndex,
       o.GraphValue AS value, o.RawComponents, o.Roles, o.SourceRowHash,
       i.GraphValue AS matched_input
FROM LTMInputEvidence i
JOIN LTMEntityEvidence o ON o.SourceRowHash = i.SourceRowHash
WHERE i.AlertTitle = %s
  AND i.Concept = 'Account_AAD_ID' AND o.Concept = 'Account_AAD_ID'
  AND i.GraphValue IN (%s)
ORDER BY o.AlertId, o.SourceRowHash, o.EntityIndex, o.GraphValue, i.GraphValue
LIMIT 501
